articles.title: Giants WR Malik Nabers says his shoulder is 'OK,' but needs X-rays; Brian Burns, Andrew Thomas injured late vs. Rams
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart wasn't the only notable Giants player injured Monday night.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers returned to Monday's 28-6 loss to Los Angeles Rams after leaving with a shoulder injury.

His was one of several injuries to notable Giants players on Monday in addition to quarterback Jaxson Dart's . Starting left tackle Andrew Thomas and All-Pro pass rusher Brian Burns left the game late with injuries long after the outcome had been determined.

Nabers told reporters postgame that his shoulder popped out and that he's scheduled to undergo X-rays. He also said that his shoulder is "OK."

"My shoulder's OK," Nabers said. "I'm gonna get an X-ray and see what's going on. … "It popped out, and I just popped it back in."

Nabers had one catch for 1 yard prior to his injury. He didn't record another catch after returning to the game with backup Jameis Winston at quarterback. His status moving forward is unclear, pending X-rays.

Nabers in pain after failing to grab 1st-quarter pass

Nabers came up clutching his right shoulder in pain after failing to grab a contested pass late in the first quarter.

He left the game, and the Giants listed him as questionable with the shoulder injury.

He continued to get work done on his shoulder by a Giants medical trainer on the ensuing Rams possession and was able to return to the field for New York's next possession with his Giants facing a 14-0 deficit.

Jaxson Dart believed to have sprained MCL

The injury to Nabers took place shortly after Dart left the game with a knee injury . Like Nabers, Dart was listed as questionable by the Giants, but he remained out of the game as Nabers returned.

Per a postgame report , X-rays were negative, and Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL. Winston took over at quarterback after Dart's injury, and the Giants failed to score a touchdown against the Rams' defense.

The Giants then sustained two more notable injuries late in the game. Thomas left New York's final possession with what the team announced as a groin injury . And Burns needed help off the field in the game's final minutes after being injured on a tackle attempt.

Burns confirmed to reporters postgame that his injury was diagnosed as a low-ankle sprain and "nothing serious."

When asked about Thomas' injury, Harbaugh said "we'll see about that" while declaring "none of these injuries are life-threatening." He didn't offer further details on Thomas' diagnosis.

The status for Burns and Thomas for Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans and beyond was not immediately clear.

It added up to a tough start for the Giants on the heels of their Week 1 upset of the Dallas Cowboys .

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes helped design a $4.26 million Kansas City compound with a Chef's kitchen, wine cellar, and a full football field in the backyard
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes is not just building a home. She is building a lifestyle around one. The $4.26 million Kansas City compound she co-designed with Patr.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes is not just building a home. She is building a lifestyle around one. The $4.26 million Kansas City compound she co-designed with Patrick Mahomes sits on a sprawling estate that reads more like a private resort than a family house. From a custom chef's kitchen built for serious entertaining to a wine cellar, a pool, and a full-size football field in the backyard, every detail in this property reflects exactly what elite NFL money looks like when it is spent with intention.What does the Mahomes' $4.26 million Kansas City home look like inside?The house itself covers roughly 7,400 square feet. That is a lot of room, but nothing inside feels wasted. Brittany reportedly had a direct hand in the design process, and that shows in how thoughtful the layout is. The chef's kitchen is fitted with top-of-the-line appliances and is clearly built for hosting large groups rather than just cooking weeknight dinners. There is a wine cellar, a home theater, and enough bedroom and bathroom space to accommodate extended family and guests comfortably.The outdoor setup, though, is where this property truly separates itself. A full-size football field behind the house. Let that land for a second. It is not a small practice patch or a trimmed lawn with yard markers painted on. It is a proper, regulation-size field where Mahomes can work on mechanics, throw routes with his kids, or just decompress between seasons. There is also a resort-style pool on the grounds, which rounds out what is genuinely one of the more impressive athlete properties in the Midwest.Brittany has been open about her interest in interior design and lifestyle branding, and this home seems to be the fullest expression of that. It is personal. It has personality. And it does not look like every other athlete mansion that gets photographed and posted online.Why did the Mahomes family invest in a custom-designed home rather than buy an existing one?The couple already owns multiple properties, so this was not a necessity. It was a choice. Building from scratch, or at least deeply customizing a compound to this level, gives them something that no pre-built home can offer: complete control over how they live.For Brittany, who has built her own public identity through fitness content, family visibility, and now business ventures, having a home that reflects her personal taste matters. It is part of the brand she has worked to build independently from Patrick's football career.For Patrick, the football field is more than a luxury. It is a working space. A three-time Super Bowl champion does not take offseason training lightly, and having that setup steps away from his back door is a genuine competitive advantage.The $4.26 million price point, while enormous by most standards, is well within reach for a quarterback on a record-breaking contract. articles.title: For more than 20 years, NFL legend Terry Bradshaw built an expansive Oklahoma ranch; years later, his 744-acre property sold for $22.5 million after becoming a major equestrian operation
articles.summary: NFL News: Terry Bradshaw spent more than two decades building something far removed from football. The four-time Super Bowl champion and Pittsburgh Steelers qua.
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw spent more than two decades building something far removed from football. The four-time Super Bowl champion and Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback-turned-Fox analyst quietly constructed a 744-acre working ranch in Thackerville, Oklahoma, near the Texas border. He called it home since 2001, breeding world-champion quarter horses and running cattle operations along the Red River. In November 2023, the ranch, valued at $22.5 million, finally sold after five years on the market, closing the chapter on one of sports' more unexpected second acts.From the gridiron to the grasslands: Terry Bradshaw's life after footballMost fans know Terry Bradshaw through the lens of Super Bowls and studio desks. But the man himself had a different vision for his post-NFL life. Bradshaw owned a 750-acre quarter horse ranch in Thackerville, Oklahoma, bordering the Red River just across the Texas state line, where he channelled the same competitive energy that made him a Hall of Famer into breeding and raising horses.This was a working cattle and equestrian operation that Bradshaw, a longtime breeder of quarter horses, built from the ground up. Not a vanity property. Not a celebrity retreat with a barn thrown in for aesthetics. This was a full-scale agricultural enterprise, and Bradshaw was involved in it the way he was involved in everything else -- completely.He told Cowboys and Indians magazine that one dream remained on his bucket list: to own 100 good brood mares. "I'm almost as enthusiastic about breeding and raising quarter horses as I was about winning my fourth Super Bowl ring," he said. That kind of dedication to a second career doesn't happen by accident. It happens over twenty-plus years of building something brick by brick, stall by stall.What 744 acres actually looks likeThe scale of the Bradshaw ranch is worth pausing on. Located about five miles north of the Red River in Love County, the property sits between Oklahoma City, 125 miles to the north, and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, just 70 miles to the south. The location was strategic. Close enough to the major markets of Texas, far enough from the noise of city life.The state-of-the-art equine breeding facility, cattle operation, and recreational ranch covered 744 acres in Thackerville, including paved roads, an 8,600-square-foot home, and several stocked fishing lakes and ponds.Inside the main residence, the design matched the man. The palatial main house boasted four stone fireplaces, wood and tile flooring, and wood paneling. A 1,000-square-foot outdoor patio area featured a full kitchen, bar, fireplace, hot sauna, and fire pit.The horse facilities alone told the story of how serious Bradshaw was about the equestrian operation. The property included a 12-stall stallion barn, a 20-stall show barn, a 20-stall weaning barn, and a 50-stall mare barn complete with an office, a laboratory, and a breeding facility. That is not a hobbyist's setup. That is a serious, professionally-run breeding operation that punched well above typical ranch weight.The ranch became internationally recognized for breeding world champion halter-class quarter horses.The Bradshaw bunch and the Ranch's double lifeAt some point, the ranch took on a second identity. The Oklahoma ranch was the filming location for the E! television series "The Bradshaw Bunch," which gave viewers a rare look at life on the property. The show ran for two seasons from 2020 to 2022, and it turned a working ranch into something of a public landmark.That visibility added an unusual layer to the eventual sale. The ranch wasn't just a piece of land with a big asking price. It had a personality, a fanbase, and a documented history that most properties simply don't carry. For buyers, that was either a feature or a complication, depending on what they wanted to do with it.Five years on the market, one failed deal, and a fresh startGetting the ranch sold turned out to be a lot harder than building it. The sale came after more than five years on the market and a previous deal that fell through.The first time around, a buyer got close and didn't follow through. Icon Global's Bernard Uechtritz said at the time: "Unfortunately, despite a series of contract extensions after repeated assurances and promises from the buyer, as well as his agents and other representatives, the buyer sadly failed to follow through, perform, fund, and close the transaction. So as of today, the entire ranch is back on the market, and it's now not a matter of if it will sell, but to whom."Bradshaw was candid about how long the decision to sell had taken. "The decision-making process to finally selling has been a long and winding road," he said. "Along the way, we have been presented with and considered many great offers, opportunities, and proposals. However, between my own schedule, the TV series, my family's changing needs, our horse and cattle business, as well as many other commitments, neither timing nor opportunity was ever on our side or completely aligned."There was more to that admission than scheduling conflicts. Among the factors that pushed Bradshaw toward downsizing was a health scare, including a cancer diagnosis. In October 2022, he publicly revealed that he had battled two separate cancers. On Fox NFL Sunday, the legendary quarterback disclosed that he had been diagnosed with bladder cancer in November 2021 and later found a Merkel cell tumor, a rare and aggressive form of skin cancer, in his neck in March 2022. He was treated at Yale and MD Anderson and declared cancer-free. "Folks, I may not look my old self, but I feel like my old self. I'm cancer free, I'm feeling great," Bradshaw said.That kind of perspective reframes why a man who built something from scratch over twenty years finally decides it's time to let it go.Who bought it, and what comes nextThe ranch sold in November 2023 to a joint venture involving Billy and Suzonne Franks from Cisco, Texas, along with Chad and Tiffany Beus, who relocated from Utah to lead the new operation.The Bradshaw Ranch has been rebranded as Red River Equine. The new owners plan to build on the foundation Bradshaw laid. The facility is being re-developed as a large-scale, premier breeding, training, and sales preparation facility catering to several different aspects of the American Quarter Horse industry. The facility will stand a variety of specialty proven stallions for breeding and provide embryo transfer as well as other niche management and breeding practices focused on augmenting alternative breeder, trainer, and competitor needs.Chad Beus stated they chose the location because of its very central geographical position to all points within the region, especially central to Texas and Oklahoma, which is important for their clientele and expansion requirements.Bradshaw, meanwhile, hasn't walked away from horses entirely. He and his wife Tammy have moved to a smaller ranch in Texas where they will continue to operate the Bradshaw Quarter Horse business. The Bradshaws had earlier moved to a smaller ranch near Saint Jo, Texas, where Bradshaw noted: "I loved this ranch so much, having built it from the ground up, so I was very tied to it."The sale price was listed at $22.5 million, though a final sale price was not disclosed by the parties involved.What the Ranch actually representsTerry Bradshaw's Oklahoma property was never a typical celebrity real estate story. It wasn't bought as an investment or a status symbol. It was built slowly, intentionally, over more than two decades by someone who genuinely wanted a different life after football.The four Super Bowls, the Hall of Fame induction, the Fox studio gig — all of that is the public resume. But the quarter horses, the breeding records, the 50-stall mare barn beside the Red River — that is what Bradshaw actually spent his adult life building when no cameras were rolling. The ranch going to new owners who plan to take the equestrian operation even further is, in some ways, the most fitting ending possible.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Zach Ertz Discusses Family's Emotional Reaction to Eagles Contract in Video After Reunion
articles.summary: Veteran tight end Zach Ertz provided some insight Tuesday into his family's response to learning he had signed on to be part of the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad.
articles.body:
Veteran tight end Zach Ertz provided some insight Tuesday into his family's response to learning he had signed on to be part of the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad.

Speaking to reporters after arriving in Philly, Ertz said his mom was "in tears," his wife was "excited," and his kids "really don't understand," although he was already teaching them to do the Eagles chant.

The 35-year-old Ertz spent parts of his first nine NFL seasons with the Eagles from 2013 to 2021.

A second-round pick out of Stanford in the 2013 NFL draft, Ertz was a three-time Pro Bowler during his time with the Eagles, and he ranks second in team history in receptions (579), fifth in receiving yardage (6,267) and seventh in receiving touchdowns (38).

Tight end became a significant need for the Eagles on Sunday when starter Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL during Philly's win over the Tennessee Titans.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport (h/t ESPN's Tim McManus ), Goedert is expected to miss "a few weeks" as a result of the injury.

The only other tight end on the Eagles' roster this season with a catch is Johnny Mundt, who has caught two passes for eight yards and is primarily a blocker.

With a pair of tight ends already on injured reserve as well in Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra, it won't be too surprising if Ertz is immediately elevated from the practice squad and playing on Monday night against the Chicago Bears.

Despite his status as a 14th-year NFL veteran, Ertz has remained productive in recent years.

With the Washington Commanders, he registered 66 receptions for 654 yards and seven touchdowns in 2024, and 50 grabs for 504 yards and four touchdowns last season.

That level of production would be more than adequate to replace Goedert temporarily, and quarterback Jalen Hurts would then potentially have a quality tight end duo at his disposal once Goedert is healthy.

articles.title: From overlooked tight end to NFL record-breaker: Travis Kelce’s 14-season journey
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s rise to NFL stardom was anything but guaranteed. Before becoming one of the Kansas City Chiefs’ most recognisable players, the tight en.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s rise to NFL stardom was anything but guaranteed. Before becoming one of the Kansas City Chiefs’ most recognisable players, the tight end faced a winding path through college football, a major setback and questions about his future in the sport. Drafted in 2013, Kelce gradually transformed himself into a game-changing offensive weapon. More than a decade later, his journey reflects persistence, reinvention and a career that continues to add new chapters.Travis Kelce’s college setback nearly changed his football futureBefore Kelce became a household name in Kansas City, his college career at the University of Cincinnati hit a major roadblock. In 2010, he was suspended from the football team after violating team rules, costing him his scholarship and putting his future in doubt.The setback could have derailed his ambitions, but Kelce eventually earned another opportunity. With support from his older brother, Jason Kelce, he worked his way back into the programme and returned to the field. The experience became an important part of his journey, showing how quickly a promising athletic career can take an unexpected turn.Kelce finished his college career with a stronger standing, recording 45 receptions for 722 yards and eight touchdowns in his final season in 2012. His performance helped put him on the NFL’s radar, even if he was not among the most celebrated prospects in the draft.The Kansas City Chiefs selected Kelce in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft, 63rd overall. It was a significant step, but his professional debut did not arrive as planned. A knee injury limited him to just one game during his rookie season, forcing him to wait before he could establish himself in the league.From a third-round pick to one of the NFL’s most accomplished tight endsKelce finally got his opportunity in 2014, and he made it count. He finished the season with 67 receptions for 862 yards and five touchdowns, giving Kansas City a glimpse of what he could become. From there, his production continued to rise, and he developed into one of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ most trusted targets.His connection with Mahomes became a defining feature of the Chiefs’ offence. Together, they helped Kansas City win multiple Super Bowls, while Kelce established himself as a consistent postseason performer. His ability to find space, make difficult catches and deliver in high-pressure moments turned him into a central figure in the team’s success.Over the years, Kelce’s numbers have placed him among the most productive tight ends in NFL history. He recorded seven consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons from 2016 through 2022, a remarkable stretch of consistency at a position known for demanding both blocking and receiving responsibilities.By September 2026, Kelce had entered his 14th NFL season with a résumé that few tight ends can match. During the Chiefs’ 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts on September 20, he caught nine passes for 101 yards and a touchdown. He also surpassed Marshall Faulk’s career yards-after-catch mark, reaching 6,288 yards.The milestone was another reminder of how far Kelce has travelled from the uncertainty of his college years. Once a third-round pick whose rookie season was interrupted by injury, he is now a record-holder whose career has spanned championship runs, individual accolades and sustained production.Kelce’s path was not a straight line to NFL greatness. It included a suspension, a lost season and the challenge of proving himself after setbacks. His story is ultimately one of persistence, opportunity and years of work. articles.title: Bills Mafia just got a new member: How one fan's ring pop moment at Highmark Stadium left 60,000 witnesses speechless
articles.summary: NFL News: Buffalo's $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium had its first regular-season home game on September 17 against the Detroit Lions, and while Josh Allen stole t.
articles.body: Buffalo's $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium had its first regular-season home game on September 17 against the Detroit Lions, and while Josh Allen stole the show on the field, one couple made sure the stands had their own headline. Gage Caldwell proposed to Sarah Cole during the Bills' long-awaited home opener, turning a historic night for Bills Mafia into something far more personal. The game ended 41-31 in Buffalo's favour. But for at least two people in that crowd, the final score was almost secondary.How did this Bills couple end up getting engaged at Highmark Stadium?Their relationship was built around this team. Cole and Caldwell have known each other since high school and have been together for about a year and a half, with Bills games woven into their dates almost from day one. "A lot of our dates have been circled around going to Bills games," Cole told WIVB. "Actually, our second date was at a Bills game."Caldwell shares season tickets with his brother. When his brother couldn't make the home opener, Caldwell saw his opening. Not just to bring Cole along, but to pop the question in the one place that meant the most to both of them. "My brother and I share the tickets, and he wasn't able to make it, so I immediately figured that she would be the one taking his spot," Caldwell said. "I knew it was going to be here at the stadium."What almost derailed the whole plan was the ring itself. Walking through security at Highmark, the diamond triggered the equipment. For a second, the surprise teetered on the edge. Then the security staff figured out what was happening and quietly waved him through. "The guys at security, they were like the best wingmen I could have asked for," Caldwell said. "Once they saw the diamond, they were like, 'Oh yeah, you're good, man. You're good.'"Cole had even sensed something was coming. "I had a thought that maybe it could happen," she said. "How cool would it be to get engaged at the first home opener at the new Highmark Stadium?" Her gut was right. When Caldwell got down on one knee surrounded by thousands of Bills fans, she said yes, even if the moment hit so hard she could barely process it. "When it happened, I blacked out, and I couldn't even remember if I said yes," Cole recalled. "I was just so happy."What makes this Highmark Stadium proposal story stand out from the usual viral moments?It wasn't staged. There was no jumbotron moment, no coordinated stadium crew, no PR setup. Just a guy with a ring, a brother who happened to cancel, and a new stadium opening its doors for the very first time. That combination is genuinely rare.The Bills won big that night, with Allen accounting for five touchdowns. But what gave this story its texture was everything before kickoff. Cole and Caldwell weren't strangers chasing a viral clip. They were two people whose relationship had grown, date by date, game by game, through Bills wins and losses. Proposing at Highmark's opener wasn't a stunt. It was the natural next step.They're planning a summer 2028 wedding. And Caldwell already has his sights on who to put on the guest list. "I have to extend the invitation to some of the Bills players, you know, whoever can make it," he said.Whether Allen RSVPs or not, the Bills already gave this couple the best possible end to their night. articles.title: Week 3 Fantasy Football Rankings for Top Players and Matchups for All Positions
articles.summary: Another week of NFL action is in the books, and fantasy managers are already looking ahead to Week 3.
articles.body:
Another week of NFL action is in the books, and fantasy managers are already looking ahead to Week 3.

Injuries to key players have clouded the fantasy landscape early in the week, as some statuses remain unclear. Jayden Daniels appears likely to miss significant time with a dislocated elbow, but Caleb Williams and Squon Barkley may be more fortunate.

Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson told ESPN Chicago (h/t NFL.com's Kevin Patra ) that Williams will be "week-to-week" with his hamstring injury. Barkley left the Philadelphia Eagles game with a stinger, and while there's no guarantee he'll start in Week 3, his injury doesn't appear to be a long-term one.

Based on what we know about the biggest injury situations, what we saw over the first two weeks of the season, and projected individual matchups, here are some early Week 3 rankings for point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Top Matchup: Patrick Mahomes at Miami Dolphins

The Miami Dolphins blew up their roster in the offseason, and after reloading with young talent, they might have the worst overall roster in the NFL. Their defense certainly didn't look good against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.

The 49ers scored touchdowns on their first five possessions before going into clock-killing mode for the remainder of the game.

Miami will provide a prime opportunity for Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to continue his return-from-injury tour. Mahomes is 100 percent healthy and has played like it. He has 566 passing yards, five passing touchdowns, 40 rushing yards, and a rushing score through the first two weeks of the season.

While there's some risk of Kansas City getting up big and going into an offensive shell early, that hasn't been an issue for Miami's opponents yet. The Dolphins have surrendered an average of 22 fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 40ers

Top Matchup: Kenneth Walker III at Miami Dolphins

Mahomes isn't the only Chiefs standout who should shine against the Dolphins in Week 3.

Kenneth Walker III has been a high-volume back for Kansas City and a centerpiece of their offense through two weeks. While the offense always flowed through Mahomes in past years, Walker has already spent time as the focal point. He's already amassed nine receptions, 369 scrimmage yards, and two touchdowns.

Walker should see a sizeable workload early against a Dolphins defense that has surrendered an average of 34.1 fantasy points to opposing backfields this season.

Top Matchup: Ladd McConkey at Buffalo Bills

Things have not gone well for the Los Angeles Chargers through the first two weeks of the season. Los Angeles' defense has seemingly regressed, and Justin Herbert seems to be still finding his footing with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

The Chargers simply haven't looked good in any facet during their 0-2 start.

About the most positive development in Week 2 was Ladd McConkey's return from a Week 1 chest injury. He caught five of seven targets for 82 yards and a touchdown during Los Angeles' 26-14 loss.

McConkey should be heavily targeted in Week 3, as the Chargers try to match points with the Buffalo Bills. Buffalo's defense has surrendered an average of 35.8 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups this season.

Top Matchup: Tucker Kraft vs. Atlanta Falcons

Tight end Tucker Kraft hasn't been as much of a focal point of the Green Bay Packers' offense as he was a year ago. While Green Bay has funneled the ball to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, Kraft has caught a modest five of nine targets for 80 yards.

However, managers should be willing to stick with Kraft on Thursday night against the Atlanta Falcons. Atlanta has been a favorable matchup for opposing tight ends during the early season, allowing an average of 17.7 fantasy points to the position.

If the Falcons are competitive enough to keep the Packers passing, Kraft should have a chance to match his combined production from Weeks 1 and 2 on Thursday night.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros.

articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: History isn't on side of 0-2 Colts and Shane Steichen. Playing it safe in OT vs. Patrick Mahomes could cost him
articles.summary: Steichen might have the hottest seat among all NFL head coaches, unless it belongs to Todd Bowles.
articles.body:
Shane Steichen failed to make the playoffs in each of his first three seasons coaching the Indianapolis Colts , and many teams wouldn't be patient enough to give him a fourth shot at it.

The Colts brought back Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard, but Colts CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it very clear that time was running out. During her postseason media conference she said: "I'm pissed. We're all pissed."

"We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher," Irsay-Gordon said.

While all teams who start 0-2 should be worried, it seems especially ominous for Steichen.

The Colts fought hard in Sunday night's game at Kansas City, but that wasn't the focus after the Chiefs won in overtime. It was Steichen's decision to kick a field goal and tie the game in overtime, giving Patrick Mahomes more than enough time to drive downfield and win it. He did, and the Colts lost 33-30 . It was the ninth straight loss for the Colts. The hot start of last season is long forgotten.

The issues in overtime started with two straight runs to Jonathan Taylor that lost 3 yards just as the Colts had driven deep into Chiefs' territory. It's reasonable considering Taylor is Indianapolis' best player, but it looked bad when the Colts suddenly faced a third-and-13.

"I was trying to finish the game with JT, put the ball in his hands," Steichen said, via the team's site .

When Indianapolis faced a fourth-and-8, there was a decision to be made. A field goal would likely result in a tie at best considering there was a little more than three minutes remaining. And the Colts, with a defense that has given up a league-worst 1,029 yards this season, gave Mahomes a chance to win with a field goal. It's not completely unreasonable to kick the field goal in that spot, but it looks bad if it doesn't work.

Steichen said the Colts were going to run a fourth-down play but only if the Chiefs lined up with a defensive look they were hoping for. When the Colts didn't like the defensive look they got, Steichen called a timeout and took the field goal.

Like the rest of Steichen's Colts tenure, it was close to being good, and that's not going to cut it. Steichen went 9-8 his first season and 8-9 in each of the two seasons after that. Last season was cruel with a 7-1 start that fell apart, especially after Daniel Jones tore his Achilles. It's clear Jones is still working back from that injury and not at his best yet, which makes it tough on the Colts and Steichen. But the NFL doesn't care much about excuses, and Steichen already got one pass for Jones' injury last season. Only 24 of 200 (12%) of teams that started the season 0-2 made the playoffs from 2002-25, according to USA Today . If the Colts don't make the playoffs for the fourth time in Steichen's four seasons, there's a good chance Irsay-Gordon will feel compelled to make a change. The odds are against him, like they were when he gave Mahomes a chance to win Sunday night.

Panic meter: Steichen might have the hottest seat among all NFL head coaches, unless it belongs to Todd Bowles.

The Buccaneers losing to the Browns on Sunday was miserable. It wouldn't have been good regardless of what came before it, but the loss being a continuation of all the Buccaneers' issues since the middle of last season is a really bad look for Bowles.

Bowles is 35-35 as Buccaneers head coach. While that's not terrible, he's trending in the wrong direction. Last season, the Buccaneers went from 6-2 to blowing the NFC South, which was one of the worst divisions in NFL history. They finished 8-9. This season they're off to an 0-2 start. Tampa Bay lost the opener at Cincinnati , and it was a winnable game if the Bucs didn't have four turnovers. They were sloppy again on Sunday against a Browns team that was blown out in Week 1, and have been sloppy in most games since that 6-2 start in 2025.

What stands out is Tampa Bay's defense let Deshaun Watson beat it. Watson had his best game, in terms of EPA per play, of his Browns career. Bowles is a defensive coach and he hasn't had a defense rank in the top half of the league in yards and points allowed since 2022.

Bowles probably was close to being fired after last season's collapse. But Tampa Bay brought him back, and the early season results are poor. Losing to the Browns has to be unacceptable. It's early in the season, but not too early to have a close eye on Bowles' job security if Tampa Bay doesn't turn things around fast.

Panic meter: The Buccaneers' next three opponents are the Vikings, Packers and Cowboys and it might be bad for Bowles to lose all three. Or maybe even two.

When a head coach fires both coordinators, there's only one more move to make if things don't turn around.

Quinn parted ways with his offensive and defensive coordinators after going 5-12 last season. The Commanders had a tough early-season schedule, starting with divisional road games against the Eagles and Cowboys. Washington went 0-2, and had a competitive loss at Philadelphia , but it's impossible to feel positive after Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow again .

Daniels injured the elbow on the final play of the first half, and he's seeing specialists before the Commanders announce a timetable for his return. If Daniels misses a month or more, what will the Commanders' record look like when he's back? And will he have a different head coach if it gets really bad?

Panic meter: Quinn might not be in immediate danger, but the seat could get hotter if Daniels misses time and the losses pile up.

Being 0-2 is bad. Being 0-2, with losses to the Cardinals and Raiders, when your next seven opponents are the Bills, Seahawks , Broncos, Chiefs, Rams, Texans and Ravens? That could be a death sentence for the Chargers' season.

The Chargers are off to a miserable start. Everything has been bad to open the season. They've lost as a big favorite twice at home and there are no positives on either side of the ball. This is really bad. It might be impossible to turn this around before it's too late.

Panic meter: An 0-9 start isn't likely, but it's not impossible either.

In the first 90 seconds of Sunday's game, receiver Jayden Reed was carted off with a back injury and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele left on the cart with a knee injury. Reed should miss time and Bako-Bewele might miss the rest of the season. It's not like the Packers' offense was in good shape before that.

The offensive line is as shaky as any in the NFL at this point. It was so thin Sunday the Packers almost had to use tight end Tucker Kraft at tackle . The line can't protect Jordan Love , who had just 145 yards passing vs. the Jets .

The running game is a mess without Josh Jacobs . MarShawn Lloyd has seemingly botched his opportunity; he was essentially benched after six carries and a fumble on Sunday. Kaleb Johnson got some extra carries, but he's far from a sure thing after the Steelers gave up on him just one year after making him a third-round draft pick.

The Packers rallied to avoid an 0-2 start. And a Thursday night game against the Falcons could be a get-right spot. But it's worrisome in Green Bay right now.

Panic meter: Getting higher and will be a five-alarm fire if they lose to the Falcons.

Mike Vrabel was just annoyed at a question after a win, but his answer to a postgame question about Maye's lackluster performance on Sunday was fairly telling.

"You're not going to ruin my Sunday, but I'll come back to you tomorrow," Vrabel said. "Thanks, bud."

Imagine Vrabel saying last season that his Sunday would have been ruined by having to talk about Maye.

Maye's slump that goes back to last postseason has been an ongoing topic, and it didn't get cured against the Steelers. Maye had 208 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. The Patriots scored just one offensive touchdown in a 20-3 win.

Maye is off to a slow start this season, as is New England 's offense. It won't be easy to break out with A.J. Brown out for a while either. But it's also not like Maye's near-MVP season didn't happen. He's a good quarterback, albeit an inexperienced one that is having to make some adjustments.

Panic meter: No reason to give up on Maye yet, but it would be nice to see a big game soon.

articles.summary: NFL News: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season did not go easy on quarterbacks. Three young signal-callers went down with potentially serious injuries in a brutal Sund.
articles.body: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season did not go easy on quarterbacks. Three young signal-callers went down with potentially serious injuries in a brutal Sunday across the league. Chicago Bears' Caleb Williams was carted off the field. Washington Commanders' Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow. New York Giants' Jaxson Dart took a nasty hit that left fans holding their breath. Several other key players also picked up injuries, painting a grim injury picture heading into Week 3.How bad is Caleb Williams' hamstring injury, and will he play in Week 3?Chicago had already been humiliated by the Minnesota Vikings on the scoreboard, managing just three points after putting up 59 in Week 1. Then it got worse. Williams scrambled outside the pocket late in the fourth quarter and crumpled to the ground in visible pain, eventually getting carted off the sideline.The Bears confirmed it is a hamstring injury and tagged him as day-to-day. Head coach Ben Johnson hasn't closed the door on Williams suiting up for Week 3, though a hamstring for a quarterback who relies on his legs is never something to take lightly. Chicago's season is young, but losing their franchise quarterback even briefly could derail whatever momentum they were trying to build.Dart's situation in New York looks more stable than initially feared. After absorbing a brutal hit in the first quarter, the Giants rookie was ruled out for the rest of the game. Early reports suggested an MCL sprain, which is obviously not ideal, but far better than the worst-case scenarios fans were imagining in real time. Dart dealt with multiple concussions in his 2025 rookie season, so any injury news around him carries extra weight. Defensive end Brian Burns also limped off late with a leg injury, leaving the Giants with some uncertainty on both sides of the ball heading into next week.What is Jayden Daniels' elbow injury prognosis, and who starts for Washington in Week 3?This one stings for Washington fans. Daniels missed significant time in 2025 with an elbow issue, and now he has dislocated that same elbow during the Commanders' loss to the Dallas Cowboys. He is already ruled out for Week 3 while doctors work through his recovery timeline. Veteran Marcus Mariota steps in as the starter in the interim.The concern here isn't just the immediate absence. It's the pattern. When a young quarterback keeps getting hurt in similar ways, it raises real questions about durability that front offices and coaching staffs have to quietly wrestle with. Daniels is talented, no question, but he needs to stay on the field to prove it.San Francisco's injury situation is becoming a crisis. The 49ers already lost Ricky Pearsall for the season and De'Zhaun Stribling for at least two months. Now wide receivers DeMarcus Robinson and Mike Evans both exited their Week 2 game against Miami. Robinson faces three to six weeks out with a high ankle sprain. Evans is dealing with a hip issue, though his outlook appears somewhat better. articles.title: Malik Nabers Injured, Latest Updates on Giants WR After Popping Shoulder Back in vs. Rams
articles.summary: Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was just one of the New York Giants' concerns in Week 2, as quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) and Malik Nabers (shoulder) suffered injuries.
articles.body:
Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was just one of the New York Giants' concerns in Week 2, as quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) and Malik Nabers (shoulder) suffered injuries.

The latter returned, though, and he told reporters after the game he popped his shoulder back into place but will still get X-rays to see the extent of the damage.

"My shoulder's okay," Nabers said. "Gonna get an X-ray on it, see what's going on. I was out there, trying to just come back out. We had lost Jax, so I didn't want to give the team another loss."

The wide receiver missed time in the first half but returned to the contest and finished with one catch for one yard.

It was a far cry from Week 1 when Nabers tallied six catches for 69 yards in a victory over the division-rival Dallas Cowboys in his first game back since September 2025 due to a torn ACL that limited him to four games last season.

His health was a major focal point for the Giants coming into the season because of that 2025 setback, although Monday's injury was an upper-body one and not the knee.

When healthy, Nabers can be one of the best receivers in the league. After all, it wasn't long ago that he was a Pro Bowler as a rookie in 2024 with 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns.

He isn't the only concern for the Giants, as ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL and is expected to miss time even though X-rays were negative.

"We'll know more [Tuesday]," head coach John Harbaugh said. "That's in the neighborhood of it. We'll get an MRI [Tuesday] and have a real good feel for it."

New York will likely rely on Jameis Winston when Dart is out, and his job will be much easier if Nabers is available. If not, Darnell Mooney and Isaiah Likely will surely see more targets in the Giants' Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: From Dianna Russini scandal to Patriots decisions, Bill Simmons questions whether Mike Vrabel has lost his ‘crisp’ edge
articles.summary: NFL News: New England picked up its first win of the season Sunday, beating the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3. But Bill Simmons did not walk away from that result fe.
articles.body: New England picked up its first win of the season Sunday, beating the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3. But Bill Simmons did not walk away from that result feeling reassured. On Monday's episode of "The Bill Simmons Podcast," the longtime Patriots fan acknowledged the defensive performance while raising something that stuck with him. Beyond Drake Maye's struggles, Simmons turned his attention to Mike Vrabel himself, questioning whether the head coach has been as sharp as the Foxborough faithful have come to expect from him.Is Bill Simmons right to question Mike Vrabel's decision-making this season?Simmons kept the tone light, but the observation landed with some weight. Referring to Vrabel as "post-Sedona Mike Vrabel," he said: "I wouldn't say he's as crisp. There's some clock management stuff that he missed today that I was like, 'Oh, Vrabel doesn't usually miss that stuff.'"The "Sedona" reference points to what became one of the NFL's most talked-about off-field stories this past spring. Photos surfaced showing Vrabel alongside NFL reporter Dianna Russini at an Arizona resort. Both initially disputed the public reading of those images. The Athletic later concluded that Russini had violated company standards by not disclosing an alleged relationship with Vrabel. The fallout was significant enough that Vrabel briefly stepped away from his duties and sought counseling. Even Russini's former podcast co-host, Chase Daniel, weighed in publicly.Simmons was not suggesting a direct line between those events and a missed timeout. His "post-Sedona" framing was clearly a joke. But underneath it was a real point. Vrabel's reputation in New England is built on precision. Game management. Situational awareness. Those are the qualities Patriots fans have trusted him for, and Simmons noticed something different in the first two weeks of this season.What do Drake Maye's early struggles say about the Patriots' offensive direction?Maye has not helped matters. Against Seattle in Week 1, he threw for 178 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions in a loss. He followed that with 208 yards and another pick against Pittsburgh. Through two games he has completed 37 of 55 passes for 386 total yards, with just one touchdown against four interceptions. Simmons called him "a mess" and pointed to underthrown deep passes and what he described as a visible drop in pocket confidence compared to last season.The bigger picture, though, is that this is not just a quarterback issue. Simmons questioned why New England has not used more two-tight-end sets or leaned on play-action more consistently. The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year. The gap between that team and what Foxborough has seen in September has been noticeable. Vrabel, for his part, kept his post-game tone measured and forward-looking. He said the formula for New England remains the same: put pressure on opposing quarterbacks and give their own quarterback a chance to play clean football.New England is 1-1. articles.summary: There's nothing quite like reaching the Super Bowl, even for a franchise that made it a habit.
articles.body:
There's nothing quite like reaching the Super Bowl, even for a franchise that made it a habit.

Video of the New England Patriots celebrating their 37-31 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC Championship Game in January 2019 circulated on social media Tuesday, and many of the dynasty's familiar faces such as Tom Brady, Bill Belichick and Rob Gronkowski play a starring role:

Rams troll Jameis, Giants on social media

Brady goes around the entire locker room and embraces with a number of people, Belichick looks far happier than he ever does on the sideline and the emotion in the room is palpable even through the screen.

Julian Edelman even told Brady, "I wanna play to make you great."

There was surely a sense of relief in the room as well considering the Patriots won the game in overtime. After Harrison Butker drilled a field goal in the final seconds of regulation to force the extra period, Brady directed a drive in overtime that Rex Burkhead capped with a touchdown run.

Burkhead also scored the Patriots' final touchdown of regulation in the fourth quarter.

Both offenses caught fire with Brady and Patrick Mahomes leading the way in that fourth quarter. New England led 17-7 after three quarters, but the game went into overtime tied at 31 before the Patriots ultimately prevailed.

New England defeated the Los Angeles Rams in the ensuing Super Bowl, giving it a third Lombardi Trophy in a five-year span. That led to another memorable celebration, but the one against the Chiefs stands out in hindsight.

articles.title: In 2012, NFL legend Jason Brown traded a $37M deal for farming; years later, his 1,000-acre farm was growing food for families who needed it most, showing his heartfelt contribution to the community
articles.summary: NFL News: Jason Brown had already reached the kind of financial success most NFL players spend years chasing when he decided to walk away from football. In 2009.
articles.body: Jason Brown had already reached the kind of financial success most NFL players spend years chasing when he decided to walk away from football. In 2009, the former St. Louis Rams centre signed a five-year, $37.5 million contract that included $20 million guaranteed, making him the highest-paid centre in the league at the time. Three years later, Brown left the NFL at 29 and moved back to North Carolina, where he and his wife, Tay, bought a 1,000-acre farm in Franklin County in October 2012.The move was not the start of another business venture built around his name. Brown had never farmed before, and he had to learn how to work the land almost from scratch. What began with a former football player trying to understand agriculture eventually became First Fruits Farm, an operation focused on growing and distributing food to people facing hunger.Jason Brown went from protecting NFL quarterbacks to learning farming from YouTubeBrown's decision to leave football came while he was still young enough to continue playing at the highest level. He later described the change as being called to a different kind of work, saying, “I was being called to a different field.”That new field was agriculture, but Brown did not arrive with years of farming experience. He had to learn everything from planting and harvesting to managing the land. According to CBS News, he even turned to YouTube to learn the basics of farming after purchasing the property.His first serious test came with sweet potatoes. Brown started with a five-acre plot, eventually producing around 100,000 pounds of sweet potatoes. Instead of treating the harvest as the beginning of a conventional farming business, he planned to give the food away through hunger-relief organisations.Brown had spent years in packed NFL stadiums and signed one of the biggest contracts ever given to a centre. Hence, this sudden shift is no doubt a shocking change. Brown was now dealing with soil, crops, weather and harvests, while trying to make sure the food reached families who needed it.Speaking about the experience of watching the crops grow, Brown said, “When you see them pop up out of the ground, man, it's the most beautiful thing you could ever see.”The first harvest also gave Brown a clearer idea of what he wanted First Fruits Farm to become. The 1,000 acres gave him the space, but the mission was not simply to put as much land as possible into production. The focus was on growing healthy food and getting it to people through food banks, pantries and community organisations.The 1,000-acre farm became much bigger than Jason Brown's first harvestThe initial numbers already showed that Brown's experiment was moving beyond a former athlete trying his hand at farming. In 2014, First Fruits Farm distributed 120,000 pounds of sweet potatoes and 10,000 pounds of cucumbers, building on the first harvest that had started with just five acres.Over time, the operation developed into a much larger food-distribution effort. First Fruits Farm's 2024 report said the organisation grew 2 million pounds of produce itself and received another 2.7 million pounds through third-party donations, allowing it to distribute a total of 4.7 million pounds of food, equivalent to about 18.8 million servings.The farm's work also expanded beyond traditional field crops. Its 2024 figures included 13,000 dozen eggs and 86,700 pounds of tomatoes and lettuce produced through its greenhouse operations. More than 20,000 volunteers contributed around 49,500 hours of work, while the organisation worked with hundreds of distribution partners.The scale grew further in the farm's reported 2025 impact figures. First Fruits Farm said it grew and distributed 7 million pounds of healthy food that year, including 3 million pounds grown on the farm and another 4 million pounds donated by outside partners. The organisation also reported more than 22,000 volunteers and 380 distribution partners. A family huddle became part of Jason Brown’s new lifeBeing away from the NFL did not mean leaving football’s lessons behind. Brown carried one of his old centre duties into family life. He used to call the huddle for his teammates. Now, he raises his fist and his eight children know to gather around him.“We’re a team. We’re a family team. We’re a farm team,” Brown said in his first-person account for The Athletic.The routine gives his children responsibilities across the farm and teaches them to work together. They have learned how to raise chickens, beef and pork, plant trees, grow gardens, hunt and fish.The reason behind Brown’s decision to leave football goes back to his older brother, Lunsford Bernard Brown II, who died while serving in Iraq in 2003. Brown was 27 when he began comparing his own life with his brother’s.“I was living a life of entertainment,” Brown wrote for The Athletic. “He lived a life of service and sacrifice.”That thought stayed with him even when three NFL teams were ready to sign him after the Rams released him in 2012. The Panthers, Ravens and 49ers were all options, but Brown chose to walk away.“Was I going to continue playing football and be self-serving? Or was I going to step out on faith and live a life of purpose?” Brown recalled.A CBS Evening News feature eventually gave him an unexpected answer to a question he had carried since leaving football. Scott Pelley introduced him as “a Hall of Famer.” Brown had never made a Pro Bowl, but hearing those words still meant something.“Everybody needs some encouragement. Everybody needs words of affirmation,” Brown wrote.His second career became more than a move from football to farming. articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. and 6 NFL Players With the Most to Prove After 2 Weeks
articles.summary: Plenty of players have begun their 2026 NFL seasons on high notes, but there are quite a few who have stumbled through the first two weeks. With Week 3 on the horizon, these struggling players are running out of time to prove themselves.
articles.body:
Plenty of players have begun their 2026 NFL seasons on high notes, but there are quite a few who have stumbled through the first two weeks. With Week 3 on the horizon, these struggling players are running out of time to prove themselves.

Whether they've had difficulty adapting to a new system or teammates, have regressed after unexpectedly strong performances last year, haven't been able to take the type of leap expected of talented young players or just can't knock the rust off after a return from injury, these declining players need to get back on track before their best campaigns become little more than statistical outliers.

With that in mind, let's highlight the six players who have the most to prove after two weeks of disappointing play.

RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Washington Commanders

Jacory Croskey-Merritt had a chance to build on his promising rookie campaign and cement his status as the Washington Commanders' feature back this year, but thus far has squandered a golden opportunity.

Croskey-Merritt flashed some real talent as a rookie in 2025, finishing the year with 805 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries. Through two games this season, JCM has recorded a pedestrian 106 yards and one touchdown on 28 totes. Most of that production came in the opener against the Philadelphia Eagles, with Croskey-Merritt getting phased out in favor of backup Rachaad White during a Week 2 meeting with the Dallas Cowboys.

NFL Network fantasy analyst Michael F. Florio broke down the most recent snap share between Washington's two backs:

Although White was expected to be more of a third-down back for Washington, he's been the more effective ball carrier through two games. White also has a stranglehold on the passing down snaps, offering far more value than his backfield counterpart in that area.

After tallying just 68 yards on nine catches last year, Croskey-Merritt unsurprisingly remains a non-factor in the passing game—reeling in just two catches that have gone for a combined negative-two yards. The addition of White, one of the league's better receiving backs, ensures that Croskey-Merritt won't see more than a token target or two per week.

With quarterback Jayden Daniels out after suffering another elbow injury, the Commanders will need to leverage their backfield platoon heavily to stay competitive. Croskey-Merritt will continue to get ample opportunity to prove himself, but he'll keep ceding snaps and carries to White if he doesn't improve his efficiency.

WR Marvin Harrison Jr., Arizona Cardinals

When the Arizona Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 draft, the club expected to get a game-changing playmaker who could anchor its WR1 position for the foreseeable future. While Harrison showed flashes of greatness during his rookie season, he regressed significantly as a sophomore and is off to an even poorer start to the 2026 campaign.

While Arizona picked up a surprising win in its opener against the Los Angeles Chargers, Harrison personally underwhelmed by catching just one of his three targets for 33 yards. That was a concerning display, but his Week 2 performance—a zero-catch, one-target showing against the Seattle Seahawks—is truly alarming.

Harrison has struggled to establish chemistry with quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who took over for Kyler Murray early in the 2025 campaign. The wideout finished last season with a modest 608 receiving yards and four touchdowns on 41 catches—a noticeable dip from the 885 yards and eight scores he recorded on 62 receptions as a rookie—and is now on a far, far worse pace.

Injuries were part of Harrison's struggles last year, as he missed five games and didn't seem close to 100 percent in several others. He appears to be healthy in 2026, however, but is failing to produce at a level even close to Cardinals star Trey McBride (17/136/2 on 23 targets), let alone unheralded teammates such as Michael Wilson (7/74/0 on 14 targets) and Kendrick Bourne (10/86/0 on 11 targets). Even backup running back Tyler Allgeier has more targets (5) and catches (4) than Harrison through two games.

While the Cardinals were able to notch a Week 1 victory without Harrison playing a significant role, the team's blowout 31-7 defeat to the rival Seahawks showed that this rebuilding organization still has a long way to go. Harrison needs to buy in and figure things out for Arizona to have any chance at emerging as a respectable offense.

The Chicago Bears have had a polarizing start to the 2026 NFL season, picking up a victory in a game that set a record for most points scored in a season-opener before suffering a humbling defeat in which they only scored a single field goal. One player who has been consistent during that span is Colston Loveland, the second-year tight end who has completely disappointed in both contests.

Although the Bears put up a whopping 59 points in Week 1, Loveland didn't record a single catch on either of his two targets. He remained a non-factor during Sunday's defeat to the Minnesota Vikings, catching just one of three targets for a lowly three yards on the day.

While Loveland also got off to a slow start and was streaky during his rookie season, this has been the least productive two-game stretch of his career and is troubling for his long-term outlook.

Loveland's fall-off looks even worse in wake of the hype he built up during the final two regular season games of 2025 when he racked up 185 yards and two touchdowns on 16 catches. The tight end followed that up with a strong playoff display that included exploding for 137 receiving yards on eight receptions to help guide Chicago to a win over the rival Green Bay Packers.

With star quarterback Caleb Williams now week-to-week with a troubling hamstring injury, it won't get any easier for Loveland to return to form. He'll need to quickly establish chemistry with backup Tyson Bagent if he's going to make any sort of impact when the Bears take on the Philadelphia Eagles in a pivotal Week 3 matchup.

Drake Maye led the New England Patriots to a 14-3 record and Super Bowl berth in his second NFL season, but the first two weeks of the 2026 campaign have seen the young star regress heavily from that MVP-caliber performance.

Maye floundered through a disappointing Super Bowl rematch against the Seattle Seahawks, throwing three interceptions (including one that sealed up the loss) and taking three sacks in a 13-10 defeat. While the Pats bounced back to get a much-needed win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, the signal-caller went just 14 of 22 on his passing attempts for 208 yards and an interception.

Considering Maye was the second-highest scoring quarterback in fantasy football last year—averaging 21.1 points per game—and is currently the QB29 with a pitiful 10.9-point average, it's clear that the 24-year-old isn't playing at the level fans in New England have become accustomed to.

Maye needs to right the ship quickly, as the Patriots face a much tougher schedule than the one they waltzed through on their way to the AFC's No. 2 seed last year. His next opportunity to get back on track will be in Week 3 when New England goes head-to-head with the Jacksonville Jaguars and their tenacious defense.

There were sizable expectations for Kyle Pitts Sr. in wake of the 88-catch, 928-receiving yard, five-touchdown season he had in 2025 and the coinciding blockbuster contract extension he received, but so far the veteran tight end hasn't come close to achieving them.

Pitts put absolutely nothing on the stat sheet in Week 1 outside of a single target during a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. While he finally got involved as a pass-catcher during Sunday's humiliating 34-3 defeat to the Carolina Panthers, he still only tallied 15 receiving yards after securing just one of three targets.

Although Pitts isn't completely at fault for this lack of production, he wasn't doing enough to make life any easier for quarterback Cooper Rush, Atlanta's third-stringer turned unexpected starter for the last two weeks.

There is hope for Pitts—who was the No. 2-scoring tight end in fantasy football last year—to get back on track. Michael Penix Jr., the starting QB for nine of Pitts' games last year, will finally be making his anticipated return to the field in Week 3.

While Penix's play over his first two seasons doesn't indicate he'll play the role of franchise savior—especially after sustaining another major knee injury—he could at least give Pitts and the rest of Atlanta's flailing passing attack a much-needed shot in the arm. If Pitts can't get it going with Penix under center, he'll be well on his way to a career-worst season.

The Cleveland Browns were willing to part ways with Myles Garrett shortly after he earned Defensive Player of the Year honors and set the single season sack record largely because they were able to return Jared Verse in addition to draft capital. While the up-and-coming edge rusher wasn't expected to seamlessly fill the enormous void left by Garrett's departure, Verse's performances over the first two weeks have looked nothing close to those of his predecessor.

Verse struggled to get going in a disheartening 34-10 Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, finishing the game with four tackles (one for a loss) and little else. Despite playing the same 64.9 percentage of defensive snaps in Week 2, Verse made even less of an impact against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Browns managed to secure a 23-19 victory, but their top edge rusher recorded one meager tackle and QB hit in the contest.

With Verse failing to record a single sack over his first two games in a Browns uniform, it's fair to start wondering if his Pro Bowl production was mostly a product of the Los Angeles Rams' creative scheming and superior talent in the defensive trenches. The edge defender had earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors after tallying 4.5 sacks and 66 tackles in 2024 and went on to improve his sack count to 7.5 while earning a second consecutive Pro Bowl nod last season.

Verse admitted that he couldn't get into a "flow state" in his Cleveland debut, revealing that he was "trying to force too much" and played outside his comfort zone. Unfortunately for the Browns, the 25-year-old was stonewalled by Tristan Wirfs in Week 2 and is now in a full-blown tailspin going into a critical Week 3 clash with the Carolina Panthers.

If Verse can't pick up his first sack of 2026 against a mediocre offensive line that has allowed QB Bryce Young to be brought down four times over the first two weeks, he may never reach the level of play the Browns expected when they traded for him.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart walks off field after injury, creating an instant contrast to Caleb Williams' emotional exit
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart walked off the field after a reported MCL knee injury, while Caleb Williams was carted off sobbing over a Grade 1 hamstring strain.
articles.body: Two franchise quarterbacks suffered lower-body injuries in Week 2. One went down with a reported MCL injury to his left knee that could result in him being sidelined for weeks, while the other suffered what is being described as a Grade 1 hamstring strain and, as of this writing, has yet to be ruled out for his team's Week 3 contest. If you had to guess which of the two quarterbacks walked off the field and into the locker room on his own power, you'd go with the second quarterback. If you were forced to pick which of the two was carted off the field and sobbed with a towel over his head, you'd understandably go with quarterback number one. And you'd be wrong. GIANTS' JAXSON DART TRIED TO REENTER GAME WITH KNEE INJURY BUT HAD JERSEY TAKEN AWAY: REPORTS New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart took an awkward, mid-air hit during the first quarter of his team's eventual loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night and did not return to the game. His left knee was forced into a position that knees are not meant to be in, and it was later reported that he was dealing with an issue with his MCL. While early reports indicate that Dart and the Giants have avoided a worst-case scenario with the knee injury, it was a gruesome sequence, but it didn't stop the second-year signal caller from walking off the turf with a slight limp. A quarterback showing his toughness and walking away after a painful injury is a common occurrence, but given what transpired with Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams less than 24 hours earlier, Dart walking off the field created quite the juxtaposition. Williams went down with a non-contact injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday afternoon, and based on his reaction in real time, it was very easy to assume he had suffered a very serious injury. Williams reached back and grabbed his left leg as he slid to the turf, a typical sign of an Achilles injury, and then rolled around on the field, screaming in pain. The former USC star was then helped onto the back of a medical cart to be taken off the field. As soon as it was revealed that Williams had suffered what was more or less just a pulled hamstring, the emotional scene instantly turned into an all-time great sports meme with folks across social media ripping into the face of the Bears franchise. articles.title: Sean McVay offers self-deprecating 'dropped mic' response as Los Angeles Rams are back in Super Bowl chase
articles.summary: Sean McVay called himself a "dumbass coach" over the Rams' Australia travel plans that preceded their blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams won their first game of the season Monday night and that allows coach Sean McVay to stop beating himself up about the season-opening loss in Australia. McVay, you should know, had been stewing about that loss to the San Francisco 49ers abroad for going on two weeks leading up to Monday night's game. He took it personally, and blamed himself, maybe because he recognized he was part of the problem. McVay finally confessed to that after beating the New York Giants in a game his team showed much more energy and better execution. RAMS' DISASTER IN AUSTRALIA RAISES THE QUESTION: SHOULD THE TEAM HAVE FOLLOWED THE 49ERS THERE EARLIER? Why? "We have the right people," McVay said. "Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. Sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot. "So there you go. That's a dropped mic." There it is: The haunting trip to Australia, with its unorthodox travel planning, is now in the rearview mirror. The Rams see themselves back on course as a Super Bowl contender. It wasn't, excuse the metaphor, an easy road to recovery because McVay took a while to let go of the Australia experience. He criticized himself afterward for days. He didn't like the way he coached and said, "I didn't do a good enough job getting us ready to go." And days later, McVay's simmering frustration boiled over when he turned his ire on the country where the game was played. "We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope," McVay told reporters. "Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere; that'll get taken out of context." The context is McVay was unhappy with the Rams' travel schedule. And he was unhappy with himself because he had a hand in setting that schedule and definitely was responsible for approving it. The Rams flew 16 hours to Australia and played the 49ers the following day. The team flew overnight out of Los Angeles on Tuesday and landed in Melbourne on Thursday morning local time. The game was played Friday morning local time. NFL ALLOWS STOLEN LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DISGUISED AS A WELCOMING CEREMONY BEFORE AUSTRALIA GAME McVay's goal was to outrun the jet lag by staying completely on Los Angeles time, playing, and immediately flying back home. The 49ers, also a West Coast team, handled it differently. They arrived in Australia six days prior to the game as part of an acclimation strategy. San Francisco 27. Los Angeles 7. The anger, the criticism, and the frustration of missing an opportunity have faded after a victory over the Giants. The players are happy about that. And they're happy to be home. "I thought our guys came out and played great," quarterback Matthew Stafford said. "We played with a bunch of passion, energy, excited to be back home in SoFi." articles.title: Drew Brees Clarifies Broncos Comeback Rumors, Says He Reached Out After Bo Nix's Ankle Injury
articles.summary: When the Denver Broncos were trying to figure out their quarterback situation going into the AFC Championship Game last season, it was Drew Brees who reached out to them about potentially making a comeback.
articles.body:
When the Denver Broncos were trying to figure out their quarterback situation going into the AFC Championship Game last season, it was Drew Brees who reached out to them about potentially making a comeback.

Amid some confusion about which side first had interest in a potential union, Brees clarified on the Let's Go podcast (h/t Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio ) he initially contacted then-Broncos assistants Pete Carmichael Jr. and Joe Lombardi to pitch the idea of potentially returning in the playoffs after Bo Nix injured his ankle:

"The thought crossed my mind to the point where I got up the next day after — here's the story. So I get the knock [from the Hall of Fame], I get the knock literally on Monday, January 19th. It was the day after the divisional round where the news had come out that Bo Nix had hurt his foot, he was gonna be out. So Jim Porter, who's the president of the Hall of Fame, we're there, we're having this moment. Dan Fouts is telling me I'm in the Hall of Fame. And I look at Jim Porter and said, 'Well, I guess this means I can't go back and play for the Broncos this week.' And he goes, 'Actually, you can do whatever you want.' He said, 'Voting's already been done, you're in, you can do whatever you want.

"And so I'm telling you when I say I like flipped the switch, I flipped the switch. Immediately texted Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi, my OC and quarterback coach with the Saints, they were with the Broncos. I said, 'You guys need me this week?' I said, 'I might be able to be ready.' And they're like, 'Are you serious? We'll go down and tell Sean [Payton] right now.' I said, 'Wait, let me get up tomorrow. Let me give this thing a go.' So I got up the next morning and I gave it a go. I had my 13-year-old son catching balls for me in the backyard. And man, it just was not happening with the right side. Left side, inside the 20 I would have been lethal. At least could have gotten them in and out of the right plays. But no, it wasn't going to happen."

There had been some confusion over who initiated the contact between Brees and the Broncos when the story was first reported last week.

Brees told NFL insider Ed Werder on Sept. 15 that Broncos coaches contacted him about potentially playing.

Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters later that same day he "never heard anything" about Brees wanting to suit up until well after the fact.

"I just know that I was the odd man out," Payton said. "I never heard anything about it. It never came to anything. I was only told about it later, so I was just like you guys."

Brees and Payton were together for 13 seasons with the New Orleans Saints from 2006 to 2011 and 2013 to 2020. Brees had a 151-94 record with the Saints between the regular season and playoffs, leading the team to a victory in Super Bowl 44.

Brees likely wouldn't have been eligible to play for the Broncos even if he wanted to.

Florio noted Brees remains on the New Orleans Saints' reserve/retired list, and NFL rules require a retired player to return by the Tuesday after Week 13 to be eligible to play.

Since the Saints still maintain Brees' contractual rights on the reserve/retired list, they also would have had to release him to clear the way for him to sign with Denver even if he had been eligible.

The Broncos wound up starting Jarrett Stidham in the AFC Championship Game against the New England Patriots. It was Stidham's first career playoff start and first start at any point since Week 18 of the 2023 season.

Stidham finished 17-of-31 for 133 yards with one touchdown, one interception and one lost fumble. The Broncos lost 10-7, marking their lowest point total of the 2025 season.

articles.title: Wherever John Harbaugh goes, QB injury concerns follow: From Lamar Jackson to Jaxson Dart
articles.summary: NFL News: The head coach or offensive coordinator calls the play and relays it to the quarterback through a helmet radio. The communication system shuts off whe.
articles.body: The head coach or offensive coordinator calls the play and relays it to the quarterback through a helmet radio. The communication system shuts off when the play clock reaches 15 seconds. From that point on, the quarterback must rely on his own judgment to execute the play.If he spots a defensive alignment that could disrupt the original call, he can change the play at the line of scrimmage. That’s what makes Russell Wilson’s Super Bowl XLIX interception so intriguing.Could he have audibled out of the pass that ended Seattle’s hopes of winning back-to-back Super Bowls? Perhaps. But he trusted the play call, and the rest is history.Now, here’s another question: Why do quarterbacks under John Harbaugh keep finding themselves in the injury conversation? Lamar Jackson dealt with injuries during his time with the Baltimore Ravens, and now Jaxson Dart has suffered a knee injury with the New York Giants.From Lamar Jackson to Jaxson Dart - John Harbaugh faces another quarterback injury scareThe New York Giants suffered a 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a suspected sprained MCL after taking a hard hit to his left knee from two defenders after throwing a third-and-8 pass. Rams linebackers Bryon Young and Josaiah Stewart sandwiched him.After the play, Dart stayed on the ground and grabbed his left leg. He received medical attention and walked to the blue medical tent for further evaluation. He then left the tent and limped to the locker room. Veteran quarterback Jameis Winston carried forward the Giants’ offense on their second drive.X-rays were negative. But the quarterback will get an MRI on Sept. 22. The head coach, John Harbaugh, said, “We’ll know more tomorrow. That’s in the neighborhood, I would say. We’ll get an MRI [Tuesday] and have a really good feel for it, and give you more information then.”ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Dart is expected to miss some time. Will he sit out the season, or is the injury season-ending? “There’s no question. The fact that it’s not that outcome that you’re talking about - the devastating outcome - is really good news,” Harbaugh told reporters.John Harbaugh is aware of Lamar Jackson and Jaxson Dart’s dangerous playing stylesJaxson Dart got injured during a standard passing play in Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The second-year quarterback missed two games in his rookie season after sustaining a Grade 1 concussion.Harbaugh said a few months earlier that Dart plays with reckless abandon. The coach stated then that the quarterback needs to protect himself better.“He’s aware of it,” Harbaugh said. “You got a fine line. I remember hearing the same thing about Lamar [Jackson], and the same things were said about Lamar really every year, but especially after the first season - ‘It’s unsustainable the way he plays. It’s never gonna last. You’ve got to protect him. He can’t run as much.’You say something like that to Lamar, and he kinda looks at you like you’ve got three heads. It’s like, ‘No, I’m gonna play ball. I’m gonna play ball.’I just knew; I trusted that he was gonna protect himself because he wants to be out there and he wants to play, and it’s not the type of sport where you [can] put yourself in bubble wrap. You’re gonna play ball, and you’re gonna get tackled, and things can happen out there.But playing the game in a way that respects that there are other guys out there that are capable of doing damage to you when you have the ball in your hands, especially for the quarterback, is important. I trust that Jaxson Dart understands that.”As for Lamar Jackson’s injuries under John Harbaugh’s reign?
