articles.title: Forgotten 2025 Draft Pick Is Beginning to Make Impact for Chiefs
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs opened up their playbook in their Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts. They weren’t as dependent on their running game, although th...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs opened up their playbook in their Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts .

They weren't as dependent on their running game, although they still excelled in that department — racking up 152 rushing yards. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes led a reinvigorated passing attack, completing 32-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. That led to some opportunities for players who haven't previously had very many.

WR Jalen Royals Is Stepping up in the Kansas City Chiefs' Offense

After not getting a single snap on offense in Week 1, Royals played 12 against the Colts on Sunday night. The Chiefs like him as a run blocker, as he was in on several rushing plays. However, he also caught two passes, including his first career NFL touchdown on a crucial fourth-and-goal situation midway through the third quarter.

Kansas City selected Royals in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. After impressing during training camp and preseason, he sustained a knee injury that halted his momentum. Royals recorded just two receptions for four yards as a rookie, barely seeing the field. Now healthy, he is rounding back into form and earning some trust from the Chiefs' coaching staff.

Chiefs HC Andy Reid Is Getting Young Guys Involved

Reid spoke highly of Royals after the game, and joked that Royals' new haircut is what led to getting him the ball.

"He got a haircut so we decided to give him the ball," Reid said. "No, listen, he's a great kid. Never says a word. The kid is as quiet as anybody I've ever been around. He just plays hard. You saw it in the preseason, now you get to see it during the (regular) season. It was great for him."

Royals wasn't the only receiver that stepped up on Sunday night, as Tyquan Thornton made two clutch catches that helped propel Kansas City to victory. Both occurred on third-and-long plays, with one going for a 45-yard gain and the other for 30 yards. The Chiefs have now given opposing defenses more weapons to worry about other than the usual receiving suspects of Travis Kelce , Rashee Rice , and Xavier Worthy .

articles.title: Proposed Trade Has Cowboys Land Familiar $35 Million Playmaker Amid Expensive Struggles
articles.summary: It is time for the Cowboys to strike an NFL trade for a familiar playmaker. The post Proposed Trade Has Cowboys Land Familiar $35 Million Playmaker Amid Expe...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have had some ups and downs to start the NFL season, but one of the biggest surprises is that the team has been unable to run the ball effectively. Cowboys running back Javonte Williams is averaging just three yards per carry during the team's first two games.

Williams posted 12 carries for 30 rushing yards against the Washington Commanders in Week 2. The Cowboys run game struggles go beyond Williams with the offensive line's performance needing improvement as well.

Yet, the Cowboys may need to consider adding another veteran running back with a different skill set. Could Dallas explore a potential reunion with Tennessee Titans playmaker Tony Pollard ?

Williams' struggles are slightly alarming given the Cowboys signed the running back to a three-year, $24 million contract over the offseason.

Let's explore what a potential Cowboys-Titans trade could look like.

Cowboys Rumors: Time for Dallas to Make a Call to Titans on NFL Trade for Tony Pollard

Pollard is in the final season of a three-year, $21.7 million contract with the Titans. The veteran running back has earned more than $35 million over his NFL career.

Behind Pollard, the Titans have a pair of young running backs in Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singelton who the team could turn to if the franchise cut ties with the veteran. The Titans are 0-2 and could be headed for another long season.

The Cowboys should attempt to dangle a future Day 3 draft pick in a trade for Pollard. With the running back hitting free agency this offseason combined with Tennessee's slow start, the Titans could be willing to move on from the playmaker.

Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones: 'Pollard Has Burst, He Has Instincts'

One of the appeals of Pollard is the running back's ability to be utilized in the passing game. During his last season in Dallas, Pollard posted a career-high 55 catches for 311 receiving yards.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has long been an admirer of Pollard's game.

"Pollard has burst, he has instincts and he literally has the fear of the defense any time he gets hold of the ball," Jones noted in 2023, per Audacy.

The Cowboys Have the 3rd Worst Rushing Attack in the NFL

It is worth noting that trading for Pollard or another veteran does not magically fix the team's running game woes. The Cowboys are not getting enough of a push from their offensive line.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer detailed the team's lack of a run game, which is the third-worst in the NFL through the first two weeks.

"Quite honestly, we came out with a different plan. We were going to throw it around the yard, and I like that plan," Schottenheimer noted on September 21, per The Athletic's Jon Machota. "It worked good. This week we might run it around the yard.

"But at the end of the day, when you look at us, we're getting a little bit too much knock back in the backfield. We're not getting the movement at times at certain things," Schottenheimer continued.

"I do think that it's a feel thing. … There's a lot of different things. Running game sometimes takes time and I think that's kind of where we are."

articles.title: Saints Play of the Day: This 98-yard Drew Brees TD pass vs. Raiders
articles.summary: It's Raiders week. This 98-yard touchdown pass from Drew Brees to Brandin Cooks is one of the best highlight plays in series history.
articles.body:
It's time to shift gears and move on from the New Orleans Saints ' Week 2 upset win over the Baltimore Ravens . Next up are the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3, which means we're going to highlight some of the best plays the black and gold have made in their 16-game series with the silver and black. And we're starting with this 98-yard touchdown pass from Drew Brees to Brandin Cooks back in 2016.

Cooks got a step on Raiders cornerback Sean Smith that gave Drew Brees enough room to fit the pass in over the coverage; Cooks caught it in stride and used his straight-line speed to cross the field for a score. Talk about a great way to build some momentum in the 2016 season-opener.

It was a historic play, breaking a Saints record that had stood since 1967. Walter Roberts only caught 17 passes for the Saints in their inaugural season but he gained 384 yards on them, including a 96-yarder that remained the longest gain in franchise history for decades.

articles.title: NFL intends to proceed with Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil, but field will look bad on TV
articles.summary: It will be important for teams to get early access, so that they can wear the right shoes.
articles.body:
On Sunday, the Ravens will face the Cowboys at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Despite concerns regarding the quality of the field, the NFL does intend to proceed.

It's our current understanding that the game is "likely" to happen as scheduled. If/when it does, expect the field to not look great on TV.

Also, it will be very important for the teams to get early access to the field so that the players will be able to make the right decisions about footwear for the game.

How it looks and how it plays will be two different things. Some fields look bad but play fine. Some fields look fine but play poorly.

Regardless, the field for the Ravens-Cowboys game is expected to look bad — if the game goes forward. And it would be a surprise at this point if the game doesn't go forward.

The obsession with international growth is strong. And the league isn't about to let something like the quality of the grass get in the way.

articles.title: Drew Brees makes significant change to story about Broncos contact
articles.summary: Speaking on SiriusXM's "Let's Go" podcast, Drew Brees made a significant revision to the story about his playoff contact with the Broncos.
articles.body:
Drew Brees has made a significant revision to the story about his contact with the Denver Broncos during the 2025 NFL playoffs.

Speaking on SiriusXM's " Let's Go " podcast with Jim Gray, Brees said he contacted former Broncos assistant coaches Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi, not the other way around.

Ahead of Denver's season opener on Sept. 14, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Carmichael and Lombardi reached out to Brees after losing Bo Nix to a season-ending ankle injury in the divisional round of the NFL playoffs. One day later, Ed Werder reported that Brees told him the retired quarterback "was contacted by former Saints coaches on Sean Payton's staff" about playing for them in the AFC Championship game.

Payton flipped the narrative when asked about the contact, noting that it was Brees who contacted the team. Now, about a week after the initial report, Brees himself says he was the one who initiated contact.

Here are his comments from the " Let's Go " podcast:

"The thought crossed my mind to the point where I got up the next day after…Here's the story. So I get the knock (from the Hall of Fame), I get the knock literally on Monday, January 19th. It was the day after the Divisional Round where the news had come out that Bo Nix had hurt his foot, he was gonna be out. So Jim Porter, who's the president of the Hall of Fame, we're there, we're having this moment. Dan Fouts is telling me I'm in the Hall of Fame. And I look at Jim Porter and said, "Well, I guess this means I can't go back and play for the Broncos this week." And he goes, "Actually, you can do whatever you want." He said, "Voting's already been done, you're in, you can do whatever you want." And so I'm telling you when I say I like flipped the switch, I flipped the switch. Immediately texted Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi, my OC and quarterback coach with the Saints , they were with the Broncos. I said, "You guys need me this week?" I said, "I might be able to be ready." And they're like, "Are you serious? We'll go down and tell Sean [Payton] right now." I said, "Wait, let me get up tomorrow. Let me give this thing a go." So I got up the next morning and I gave it a go. I had my 13-year-old son catching balls for me in the backyard. And man, it just was not happening with the right side. Left side, inside the 20 I would have been lethal. At least could have gotten them in and out of the right plays. But no, it wasn't going to happen."

Why does it matter? Because Brees was technically still on the New Orleans Saints ' reserve/retired list, the Broncos contacting him technically could have been tampering, which could lead to NFL discipline . The league might have more grace for the "tampering" if it was Brees who initiated the contact. The NFL declined to comment on the matter, which might be a sign that they're treating it as no big deal.

In the end, nothing came of it because past shoulder and wrist injuries prevented Brees from attempting a comeback at age 47.

"[M]y right wrist, right shoulder wouldn't allow it to happen," Brees said on the podcast . "But did I think about it? Absolutely. 1000%. I would've loved to come back and play for the Broncos in the AFC Championship game, get my coach and a bunch of the other guys that I know in that organization, the Penner family, to the Super Bowl. Would've loved it."

With Brees unable to play, the Broncos started Jarrett Stidham , who had two costly turnovers in a 10-7 loss to the New England Patriots . Stidham is now back with the club as their primary backup QB for the 2026 season.

articles.title: Will Levis, Jets Reportedly Agree to Contract, Will Be QB3 Behind Geno Smith, Cade Klubnik
articles.summary: The New York Jets are signing quarterback Will Levis to their practice squad, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
articles.body:
The New York Jets are signing quarterback Will Levis to their practice squad, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

The team is releasing Bailey Zappe to open a spot for the 2023 second-round pick. The Jets have two QBs, Geno Smith and Cade Klubnik, on their active roster.

Levis made 21 starts across his first two seasons with the Tennessee Titans. He threw for 3,899 yards, 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions. His tenure in Music City was marked by some inexplicable decision-making.

The 27-year-old missed all of 2025 due to shoulder surgery, and the Titans waived him in August.

Levis' fall out of the first round was one of the biggest storylines from the 2023 draft. He wound up justifying all of the concerns people had about his game coming out of college.

Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones are two quarterbacks who shed their label of being a draft bust and found success with a change of scenery. In the case of Levis, though, it's difficult to find any hidden upside. His 25.2 QBR was last among qualified passers in 2024, per ESPN.com .

Since then, Levis has missed an entire year of development time.

From New York's perspective, there isn't much risk in bringing him onto the practice squad. Maybe Levis has something in his arsenal he didn't show with the Titans.

And if push comes to shove and the Jets have to elevate their third-stringer to the starting job, he at least has some experience in the role.

articles.title: Eagles Reportedly Sign Kenny Moore II, Full Contract Details Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are signing cornerback Kenny Moore II to their practice squad, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are signing cornerback Kenny Moore II to their practice squad, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Moore is getting a one-year deal worth as much as $3 million.

The Indianapolis Colts released him in May after failing to find a trade that suited both parties. He started 14 games for the team in 2025, finishing with 55 tackles, one interception and six pass breakups.

Moore was a Pro Bowler in 2021, but that season is an outlier in his NFL career. For the most part, he has been a solid defensive back without consistently hitting a high level.

The writing was on the wall as it related to his future in Indy because he had slipped in and out of a starting role in 2025. He was on the field for 76 percent of the team's defensive snaps, his lowest rate since 2017.

Versatility is a strength for Moore because he lined up in the slot and on the outside with the Colts. That could help him carve out a role in a secondary that has no shortage of options.

Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean were both All-Pros a season ago, and Riq Woolen is entrenched as a starting boundary corner opposite Mitchell. The Eagles also have veterans Michael Carter II, Jonathan Jones and Kelee Ringo in the fold alongside safeties Andrew Mukuba and Marcus Epps.

Through two games, Philly is tied for the fifth-fewest passing yards allowed at 166 per contest.

Having a corner with Moore's track record so far down the depth chart is a nice luxury for the Eagles.

articles.title: Seahawks' Macdonald Says Sean Payton Was Unhappy with Use of Video from Broncos' Public Practice
articles.summary: There was a time during the 2024 NFL season that Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton wasn't pleased with Seattle Seahawks, according to Mike Macdonald.
articles.body:
There was a time during the 2024 NFL season that Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton wasn't pleased with Seattle Seahawks, according to Mike Macdonald.

During an undated interview with Graham Bensinger that was released this week, the Seahawks head coach revealed that his Seattle team partially scouted the Broncos by using training camp clips fans posted on their public social media accounts.

"We took like 100 plays from their training camp," Macdonald said before explaining that cooler heads eventually prevailed. "… He got wind of it and he like lost it. This was the middle of the season."

Seattle defeated Denver 26-20 in the 2024 opener for each team.

The Seahawks picked off Bo Nix twice and held the Broncos to just 4.0 yards per carry on 25 rushing attempts. They were up double digits until Nix scored a rushing touchdown with fewer than three minutes remaining, although Denver never got the ball back after that score.

To be sure, Macdonald is not the first coach to try to gain an edge by culling through social media clips.

Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters earlier this month about a conversation he had with Dolphins passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo regarding a 2024 game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Green Bay Packers.

Patullo was on Philadelphia's staff at the time, while Hafley was on Green Bay's. Hafley said that Patullo revealed to him the Eagles had half of Green Bay's blitz packages because of publicly posted videos from fans at training camp:

Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who was also on Philadelphia's staff at the time, previously warned against allowing fans to record practice footage.

If nothing else, teams may be more vigilant in the future about allowing fans to record their training camp practices given some of the recent comments from coaches around the league.

articles.title: Zach Ertz, Eagles Agree to Contract for Reunion After Goedert Injury, Updated Depth Chart
articles.summary: Zach Ertz is returning to the City of Brotherly Love.
articles.body:
Zach Ertz is returning to the City of Brotherly Love.

The veteran tight end has signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, with ESPN's Adam Schefter reporting he is expected to join the practice squad.

He likely will see the field before long with Dallas Goedert expected to miss several weeks after suffering a sprained MCL on Sunday. In fact, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reported Ertz is expected to play against the Chicago Bears on Sept. 28.

Ertz will join a tight end room that currently includes Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins with Goedert injured and rookie second-round pick Eli Stowers on injured reserve.

The 35-year-old suffered a season-ending ACL tear in early December, calling into question whether it would be the final moment of his career.

"It breaks my heart when you see a great one like him, an all-time great [get hurt]," Washington Commanders tight end John Bates told reporters after Ertz's injury. "He does everything the right way, the way things should be done. He's just a pro's pro."

"He's one of the linchpins of our team," Terry McLaurin added. "I ain't going to lie; it was tough for everybody."

After going through injury rehab, his knee doesn't appear to be a concern at this point:

Ertz has 825 career receptions, the fifth most by a tight end in NFL history. His 116 receptions in the 2018 season with the Eagles was also a single-season NFL record for tight ends before Arizona's Trey McBride broke it this year.

He's added 8,592 receiving yards and 57 touchdowns across 13 seasons in stints for the Eagles (2013-21), Cardinals (2021-23) and Commanders (2024-25).

He recorded 50 catches for 504 yards and four touchdowns across 13 games in 2025. Philly clearly believes he can still be a contributor and needs the help at the position given their early injuries.

articles.title: Simone Biles' Husband Jonathan Owens Reveals Reaction to 'Mr. Biles' Remarks by Social Media Trolls
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts defensive back Jonathan Owens isn't offended when people make jokes that he is less recognizable than his wife, Simone Biles.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts defensive back Jonathan Owens isn't offended when people make jokes that he is less recognizable than his wife, Simone Biles.

In fact, he sees it as a sign of respect.

"I take it as respect," he said, per Candace Buckner of The Athletic. "You see who my wife is. Says a lot about me as well. Like, my confidence, and who I am as a person that she chose to be with me. It's respect, because as a man in this field, (one of the) things they judge you on is who is your significant other. That says a lot about your confidence."

Buckner noted Owens has his social-media notifications turned off, so he likely isn't going to see any jokes calling him Mr. Biles even if fans are making them.

Owens has reached the highest level of his sport during a career that features stops with the Houston Texans, Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears and now Colts. He even posted 125 tackles during the 2022 campaign with the Texans and returned a fumble recovery for a touchdown in 2023 with Green Bay.

However, he isn't on the level of Biles.

And that is because only a select few athletes in any sport have ever come close to reaching her level.

Biles is widely considered the greatest gymnast in history and even has a number of official moves named after her. Her resume includes seven Olympic gold medals, two silver medals and two bronze medals.

She competed in the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Games and captured three golds in the most recent ones in Paris.

Owens may be more recognizable because of his wife's accomplishments than his own, but that says far more about her gymnastics career than it does his football one.

articles.title: Tyson Bagent Injured, New Bears Rumors Ahead of Eagles Game Amid Caleb Williams Hamstring Issue
articles.summary: Caleb Williams' hamstring isn't the only injury the Chicago Bears have to worry about heading into their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams' hamstring isn't the only injury the Chicago Bears have to worry about heading into their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that backup quarterback Tyson Bagent is in the NFL's concussion protocol, which means third-stringer Case Keenum may be tasked with taking the field against the Eagles on Monday.

Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and Bagent entered the game in the fourth quarter with the team trailing.

He had an opportunity to win it, but the offense stalled ahead of a blocked field goal on his first possession. It then moved into the red zone in the final seconds trailing by six only for it to turn the ball over on downs on the final play of the 9-3 loss.

Still, having more than a week to prepare for the Eagles alongside head coach Ben Johnson figured to put Bagent in a better spot to succeed than when he was thrown into the fourth quarter of a divisional showdown in rainy conditions.

Yet those plans are apparently on hold as he is in concussion protocol, leaving Chicago's quarterback situation tenuous at best.

Keenum is a veteran who has 66 career starts during a career that includes stops with the Houston Texans, St. Louis/Los Angeles Rams, Vikings, Denver Broncos, Washington, Cleveland Browns and Buffalo Bills.

But he hasn't started a game since he went 1-1 during the 2023 campaign. Starting him against a playoff contender such as the Eagles was not in the cards for the Bears heading into the season.

Ultimately, Chicago's long-term outlook for the season depends on Williams' status. Johnson said he is considered "week-to-week," although Rapoport noted he will "likely" be out against Philadelphia.

If Bagent is out as well, the Bears will be staring at an uphill battle in their next game.

articles.title: 3 key NFL quarterbacks suffered injuries in a brutal Week 2. Here’s the latest on their status
articles.summary: The second week of the NFL season proved to be a brutal one for three young quarterbacks who were expected to take major leaps this season.
articles.body: The second week of the NFL season proved to be a brutal one for three young quarterbacks who were expected to take major leaps this season. Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears, Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders and Jaxson Dart of the New York Giants were all knocked out of their Week 2 matchups with injuries that looked to be serious. Williams went down with a no-contact injury during the Bears’ loss to the Minnesota Vikings, being carted off the field as medical staff paid close attention to his right leg. Daniels dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys. And in the Monday night game, Dart suffered a brutal looking knee injury when he was hit by two Los Angeles Rams defenders as his team fell in LA. Dart’s injury, in particular, might end up being the most concerning. Three young stars, three injuries that could have outsized effects on the NFL season. Here’s what we know about their status right now. Caleb Williams The Bears quarterback might actually be in the best shape out of the trio of injured QBs, even if his injury appeared to be the most serious in the moment. Late in the Bears’ miserable offensive showing against the Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field, Williams was attempting to score the game’s first touchdown in the fourth quarter. On a first-and-goal play from the 6-yard line, Williams faked a handoff and wheeled around to his left. As he pointed to a receiver in the end zone and eluded a diving Vikings defender, Williams suddenly crumpled to the ground. He slid on the wet turf and began screaming in pain as he rolled around. The 2022 Heisman Trophy winner was eventually carted off with a towel over his head, giving a raised fist to the crowd. The immediate reaction among Bears faithful was concern that their signal-caller would be out of the lineup for a lengthy period of time. On Monday, head coach Ben Johnson said Williams appears to have escaped a worst-case scenario. Mike Florio, NBC’s NFL Insider, said ahead of the Sunday night game that he was hearing Williams suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain, the lowest level of hamstring injury. Johnson said on Monday that the quarterback will be week-to-week and isn’t being ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. “He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here,” Johnson said in the news conference, according to the Bears’ website. “We’ll see what that looks like. Here’s what I know: This guy’s a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night. I’ll double down on that. He gets back – he has in the past – a lot faster than what people can anticipate. I’m not putting a timeline on this. We’re going to say week-to-week. He’s going to attack this with everything that he knows. He’s got a great team around him, both in this building and outside this building, and we’ll see where it goes from there.” If Williams can’t play, Tyson Bagent will take over quarterback duties for the Bears after finishing out Sunday’s game against the Vikes. Jayden Daniels The Commanders’ star quarterback does not appear to have been so lucky. Daniels took a snap close to the Cowboys’ end zone on Sunday and stumbled to the ground, putting his left arm out to brace himself as he fell. As it hit the ground, his elbow buckled and Daniels stayed down in considerable pain. After the game, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Daniels dislocated his elbow and an X-ray showed no fracture. “I was just disheartened for him. Like, I know what he’s gone through to go,” Quinn said. “He’s in good spirits tonight. Just knowing that, like, we wanted to all play so well for him in that space. And so, to see him in that spot, it stunk for the guys and I thought Marcus (Mariota) did a really good job coming back in when we were starting on offense, then we get going, right off the bat – it was tough.” It’s a particularly difficult moment for Daniels after an injury-plagued 2025 season that included missing multiple games after he dislocated the same elbow in a game against the Seattle Seahawks. He returned in a game against the Vikings and then reaggravated the injury, leading to him missing the rest of the season. The promising Commanders leader, who helped guide his team to the NFC championship game in the 2024-25 season, missed 11 games last season. There were no further updates on Daniels’ status on Monday from Quinn as he continues to seek opinions on how long he’ll be out. Mariota will take over the starting job going forward until the former LSU standout and 2023 Heisman winner can return. It’s a brutal moment for the Commanders as they looked to shake off a disappointing 2025 season and get back to the great vibes that followed the team in 2024. Daniels’ emergence as a star brought back memories of Robert Griffin III’s time in Washington, when he sparked a similar football renaissance in the nation’s capital. The two are similar players in that they have cannon arms but also the speed and escapability that give opposing defenses fits. RGIII’s time in Washington ended after he suffered multiple career-altering injuries. Commanders fans will be dreading the idea that Daniels might be suffering a similar fate. Jaxson Dart The New York Giants were looking forward to a new season under head coach John Harbaugh, a name synonymous with winning in the NFL and Dart was expected to be a key player in their resurgence. All that is up in the air now. As Dart dropped back to pass during the opening drive of Monday’s game, he was hit in the backfield by two converging Rams pass rushers. In an awkward-looking collision, one of those Rams – Josaiah Stewart – collided with Dart’s lower body. The hit caused his left knee to bend sideways. Not the way knees are supposed to bend, to say the least. Dart went down quickly and was in obvious pain but was able to walk off the field under his own power. Harbaugh said after the game that Dart being able to walk off the field – and he’d return to the sidelines in street clothes later – meant the worst possible scenarios seemed to have been avoided. “The fact that it’s not that outcome that you’re talking about, the devastating outcome, is really good news,” Harbaugh said, adding that more imaging would be done on Dart’s knee on Tuesday to figure out the extent of the injury. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network reported that the QB is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL, which would likely mean he’d miss time. Harbaugh would not confirm whether the team anticipated having Dart out for Week 3’s game, only saying that he was waiting on follow-up tests before making a decision. Rapoport and others reported on Tuesday that the good signs from Monday night might not actually have been all that real. Reports on Tuesday afternoon indicated that Dart’s injury is worse than initially believed and that he could be out for a prolonged period of time. Rapoport said it’s possible he may even miss the rest of the season. Dart is another player who was hoping to move past an injury-plagued 2025, having missed multiple games with a concussion during his rookie season. Jameis Winston took over quarterbacking duties once Dart went down and would be named the starter if he misses any time. When asked after Monday’s game if he was preparing to be the starter going forward, Winston instead focused on Dart. “My role is to keep him lifted up, keep this team motivated and put this game behind us, find ways to be solution-oriented and have a better week of preparation, a better game of efficiency, and overall get a win,” Winston said.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Announces 'Patient Zero,' 1st Single Since Wedding to Travis Kelce
articles.summary: It didn't take long for Taylor Swift to reveal the answer to the easter eggs that had recently been planted.
articles.body:
It didn't take long for Taylor Swift to reveal the answer to the easter eggs that had recently been planted.

Swift announced her new single "Patient Zero" will be available on Friday.

Tuesday's announcement comes after the famously eagle-eyed Swifties noticed the pop-music superstar had changed the written lyrics on streaming platforms from some of her already-released music to replace the letter "O" with the number "0" in spots.

"Patient Zero" will mark Swift's first new release since her wedding to Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce on July 3. It will be her second single of the year after "I Knew It, I Knew You" from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack.

There is no confirmation of a full album at this point, but Swift has released at least one album every year since 2019. This includes re-recordings of her old albums.

articles.title: Giants' Top QB Trade Targets, NFL Free Agency Options After Jaxson Dart Injury
articles.summary: It turns out the New York Giants might not have Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the season after he suffered a knee injury in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
It turns out the New York Giants might not have Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the season after he suffered a knee injury in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , Dart's MRI revealed his knee injury is "worse than anticipated" and it could keep him out for the rest of the season.

Dart was injured on the final play of New York's opening possession when his knee ping-ponged after being hit by Rams linebacker Byron Young, then into linebacker Josaiah Stewart.

Jameis Winston took over for the rest of the game, finishing 11-of-27 for 111 yards and one interception.

Since the Giants are playing on a short week going into Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, Winston will almost certainly get the starting nod.

Beyond that, though, the Giants could at least explore trade and free-agent targets in an attempt to salvage their season with Dart out for the time being. Winston didn't look like viable long-term option, albeit in a tough assignment against a good Rams defense even without Myles Garrett on the field.

Here are some potential quarterback options the Giants could look at if they want to add more depth since Dart and Winston were the only signal-callers on the active roster for the first two games.

Of the current free-agent options, Jimmy Garoppolo is the most accomplished with a 43-21 career record in 64 starts.

There was speculation early in the offseason that Garoppolo was considering retirement, but NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported in July that the 34-year-old wants to keep playing if he can find the right situation.

Garafolo noted at the time nothing was "imminent" for Garoppolo, and it "might take an injury to a quarterback or the need for a veteran to get into the mix."

Well, here is an injury situation that could open the door for Garoppolo.

Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy utilizes a variation of the west-coast offense that relies on pre-snap motion, RPOs and screen passes. Those were all elements that helped Garoppolo achieve his greatest success in the NFL during his time with the San Francisco 49ers.

Even though the Giants don't have the equivalent of prime Deebo Samuel, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey to boost Garoppolo, a group of Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo is a good skill-position unit to work with.

This is a take-your-pick among whichever Philadelphia Eagles backup Howie Roseman might be willing to trade within the same division.

Tanner McKee has had a fascinating run with the Eagles since being a sixth-round pick in the 2023 draft. He had a strong 2025 preseason that led to some absurd takes about how much he would return in a trade.

As recently as March, the reported asking price for McKee was a second-round pick. After a lackluster preseason this year, he has been relegated to the emergency No. 3 quarterback behind Andy Dalton.

Given that the Eagles have kept McKee inactive for the first two games and being in the final season of his rookie contract, it might be easier for the Giants to get him than Dalton right now.

If there is a reason for the Giants to make an attempt for Dalton, it's because a member of their offensive coaching staff has familiarity with him.

Brian Callahan, the current Giants passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, worked as the Cincinnati Bengals offensive coordinator from 2019 to '23. Dalton was still with the Bengals in 2019 and started 13 games.

Dalton also has extensive experience in the NFL with 179 appearances in 16 seasons. McKee has appeared in six games over the past three seasons.

This is probably the most depressing potential option the Giants could make, but it also speaks to what the quarterback market looks like when you need one during the season.

Tua Tagovailoa was set to start for the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1 before an oblique injury suffered in practice days before the game kept him out.

The Falcons will get Michael Penix Jr. back for their Week 3 game against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night.

Despite having a healthy Penix back, the Falcons reportedly aren't looking to release Tagovailoa right now.

Tagovailoa's primary selling point in a trade to a quarterback-needy team is his low salary ( $1.2 million ) and presumably low draft pick the Falcons would want if they were to deal him.

It's also plausible that if Penix looks good as he works his way back from ACL surgery, the Falcons could end up releasing Tagovailoa and a team like the Giants could just sign him without having to give up a trade asset.

Look, this isn't a great option for the Giants if they are looking to compete for a playoff spot. But desperate times could call for desperate measures. Tagovailoa, even in a down 2025, still threw for 2,660 yards with 20 touchdowns, 15 interceptions and a 67.7 completion percentage in 14 starts with the Miami Dolphins.

For comparison, the last time Winston threw for at least 2,500 yards and 20 touchdowns in a season was 2019.

articles.title: Giants QB Jaxson Dart's knee injury reportedly worse than anticipated, possibly season-ending
articles.summary: Dart suffered the injury during the Giants' opening drive in their Monday night loss to the Rams.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could reportedly be done for the season after sustaining a knee injury during Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , the MRI results showed that the damage was worse than expected. Dart will be out for an "extended period of time" and the injury could be season-ending.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh met with reporters on Tuesday afternoon and said that Dart is continuing to be evaluated and they have not made any decisions on the quarterback's future status. The team "learned a lot more" about the injury following the MRI.

"It's an ongoing conversation about the health of a player, of a person," Harbaugh said. "We've got to prepare for the range of possibilities."

As for whether the injury could require season-ending surgery Harbaugh said, "I don't think I could really comment on that right now until we know for sure what's going to transpire."

Dart suffered the injury in the first quarter and did not return to the game. X-rays were negative and the second-year signal-caller underwent an MRI on Tuesday after the team returned home from Los Angeles .

During the game's opening drive, Dart dropped back to pass and jumped to make a throw downfield while under pressure. He was sandwiched between Rams linebackers Josaiah Stewart and Byron Young before falling to the ground holding his left knee.

After being tended to on the field, Dart limped off and was taken for further evaluation. He was initially listed as questionable to return before being ruled out. He returned later without his uniform and watched the remainder of the game from the sideline.

Jameis Winston , who signed a two-year, $13-million extension before Week 1, finished the game going 11-for-27 with 111 passing yards, an interception and taking two sacks.

Jaxson Dart among Giants' MNF injury concerns

Dart wasn't the only injured Giant coming out of Monday night.

Left tackle Andrew Thomas suffered a groin injury on the team's final offensive play, but no update has been provided on his status.

The Giants entered the game without cornerbacks Deonte Banks and Paulson Adebo , who were ruled out due to injury.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart reportedly suffered a knee injury "worse than initially thought" and the team is bracing for the possibility he'll have to undergo season-ending surgery, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday.

Dart was initially believed to have suffered an MCL sprain after preliminary tests on Monday night.

Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters after the game that the team would "know more" on Tuesday but confirmed that he heard an MCL sprain was "in the neighborhood" of what the team believed to be the diagnosis.

Dart exited the 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in the first quarter after taking a big hit in the pocket. He suffered a left knee injury and was taken to the locker room after staying down on the field for some time before limping off under his own power.

Dart was eventually ruled out, but not before campaigning to return.

Reporting from the sideline during the fourth quarter, ESPN's Laura Rutledge said Dart didn't relinquish his uniform to the Giants' training staff until shortly before halftime ended.

As a rookie in 2025, Dart provided excitement and hope for a struggling franchise. He took over the reins of the offense in Week 4 and completed 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions in 12 starts. He also rushed for 487 yards and nine touchdowns.

Dart is the present and future in New York as the Giants look to break a malaise that's seen the team post losing records 11 times in 13 seasons.

Jameis Winston, who went 11-of-27 for 111 yards and an interception against the Rams, will be under center until Dart is healthy.

articles.body: Tom Brady spent two decades making impossible things look routine on the football field. Turns out, he might be just as dangerous in real estate. The seven-time Super Bowl champion purchased a two-acre lot on Miami's Indian Creek Island back in 2020 for $17 million. He then built a luxury compound from scratch on it. Now, according to Bloomberg, that same property is being quietly shopped to a select group of buyers, with bids already crossing the $150 million mark. That's a $133 million paper gain. Without playing a single snap.How did Tom Brady turn a $17 million lot into a $150 million mansion?Indian Creek Island isn't your average zip code. The private island off Miami Beach houses just 41 residences and counts Jeff Bezos, Ivanka Trump, and several hedge fund billionaires as neighbors. Locals call it the "Billionaire Bunker," and that nickname isn't ironic. Security is tight. Access is tighter. And real estate prices there operate by rules that don't apply anywhere else.Brady bought the land in 2020 alongside his then-wife Gisele Bündchen while he was still playing for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The lot cost $17 million. Then came years of construction. What Brady built wasn't just a house. It was a two-story waterfront compound with a state-of-the-art gym, infinity pool, sport courts, and a cabana. Every detail was custom. Every inch was intentional.He didn't flip a distressed property. He started with raw land, designed it to his exact specifications, and created something that simply didn't exist before he got there. That distinction matters. A lot.The property hasn't officially hit the market. There's no listing, no open house, no Zillow page. Bloomberg reported it's being shown privately to a small group of serious buyers. Three separate sources told the outlet that bids have already come in above $150 million. If one of those bids closes, Brady won't just be cashing out. He'll be rewriting Miami real estate history.Would Tom Brady's Indian Creek sale be the most expensive home ever sold in Miami?The short answer is yes, and it won't be close.The current record for a single-family home sale in Miami belongs to hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin, who paid $107 million for his Coconut Grove property in 2022. That was already a staggering number. Brady's potential $150 million sale would blow past it by more than $40 million.To put that in perspective, Brady has earned roughly $300 million in NFL salary across his entire career. This one property could net him half that. From a piece of land he's owned for five years.It also fits into a broader shift in his real estate strategy. Brady is currently renovating a 14,000-square-foot estate in Brentwood, California, which suggests his attention, and possibly his base, is drifting west. Selling Indian Creek would free up serious capital and close the Miami chapter cleanly.Whether that sale happens this year or not, the numbers alone tell a story worth paying attention to. articles.body:
Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Dart's injured left knee is being evaluated in the aftermath of the starting quarterback exiting the game in defeat at the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night .

Dart was hurt less than four minutes into the game while being pressured on third-and-eight.

Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut Dart's legs, resulting in a heavy fall.

Harbaugh refused to confirm reports that Dart's injury is worse than the initial diagnosis of a sprained medial collateral ligament, leading to an extended absence and possibly season-ending surgery.

After the 28-6 loss, Harbaugh said it was "in the neighbourhood" and that an MRI would lead to more information.

"It's an ongoing conversation about the health of a player, of a person," Harbaugh said. "We've got to prepare for the range of possibilities."

Harbaugh said the team would reveal details and a timeframe in due time after the evaluation is complete.

He expressed confidence in backup Jameis Winston's ability to step in for however long Dart is out.

The Giants also saw top pass rusher Brian Burns sprain his left ankle and left tackle Andrew Thomas sustain an apparent lower-body injury in the fourth quarter.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers had to pop his right shoulder back into place after dislocating it on the second-to-last play of the first quarter.

"But that's just part of football," Burns said. "Guys go down every day, and it's always next guy up. That's why you try to develop a culture where you don't slack off in production with the guys that's behind."

Harbaugh said the Giants can't get discouraged by their change in fortune.

"All around the league, everybody deals with it," he said. "This is football. This is the NFL. This is what you do. So our task is not to lament it."

Former NFL legend Adam Vinatieri is now a Guinness World Record holder.

The longtime kicker made a field goal on the Jungfraujoch—a mountain attraction nicknamed the "Top of Europe"—which sits at 11,332 feet above sea level in the Swiss Alps.

"I've had the chance to attempt a lot of special kicks in my career, but getting to go for an official Guinness World Records title on snow at 3,454 meters in a Patriots jersey is truly something special," Vinatieri said . "The conditions up there in the Alps are completely different from anything we know from the NFL. That's exactly what makes this challenge so exciting."

Vinatieri's most famous kicks also came in snow back in the controversial "Tuck Rule Game" during the Divisional Round of the 2001 season, when his 45-yard field goal in blizzard-like conditions forced overtime against the Oakland Raiders and his 23-yarder in overtime sealed the victory.

articles.title: Ravens add speedy Auburn product Shedrick Jackson to practice squad
articles.summary: The Ravens added former Raiders wide receiver Shedrick Jackson, the great-nephew of Bo Jackson, to their practice squad
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens added more speed and experience to their wide receiver depth chart.

Baltimore signed wide receiver Shedrick Jackson to its practice squad, adding another developmental option as it prepares for a Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Jackson, the great-nephew of Auburn and Raiders legend Bo Jackson, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. He spent parts of two seasons with Cincinnati before joining the Las Vegas Raiders ' practice squad in December 2024.

The 6-foot-1, 198-pound receiver made five appearances for Las Vegas in 2025, catching four of his five targets for 56 yards and one touchdown. He caught his first NFL pass and scored his first touchdown on the same play against the Denver Broncos . Speed is Jackson's most intriguing attribute. He clocked 4.25 seconds in the 40-yard dash during Auburn's pro day, giving Baltimore another receiver who can stretch coverage vertically.

Jackson appeared in 53 games over five seasons at Auburn, finishing his college career with 66 receptions for 874 yards and one touchdown. His best season came in 2021, when he caught 40 passes for 527 yards and a touchdown.

The practice-squad designation means Jackson should initially provide depth and help Baltimore's defense prepare for opposing receivers. His special-teams experience could eventually improve his chances of earning a game-day elevation.

Baltimore has dealt with uncertainty at receiver after Zay Flowers ' hamstring injury and Ja'Kobi Lane's move to injured reserve. Jackson is unlikely to impact the rotation or carve out a role, but he gives the Ravens another experienced option with legitimate NFL speed.
